TrainPipelineConfig:

  --output_dir [Path]   Set `dir` to where you would like to save all of the
                        run outputs. If you run another training session with
                        the same value for `dir` its contents will be
                        overwritten unless you set `resume` to true. (default:
                        None)
  --job_name [str]
  --resume bool         Set `resume` to true to resume a previous run. Pass
                        `--config_path` pointing at either a local
                        checkpoint's train_config.json or a Hub repo id
                        holding `checkpoints/<step>/` subtrees (the latest
                        checkpoint is downloaded and resumed from). Note that
                        when resuming, the default behavior is to use the
                        configuration from the checkpoint, regardless of
                        what's provided with the training command at the time
                        of resumption (CLI `--*` flags still override).
                        (default: False)
  --seed [int]          `seed` is used for training (eg: model initialization,
                        dataset shuffling) AND for the evaluation
                        environments. (default: 1000)
  --cudnn_deterministic bool
                        Set to True to use deterministic cuDNN algorithms for
                        reproducibility. This disables cudnn.benchmark and may
                        reduce training speed by ~10-20 percent. (default:
                        False)
  --tf32 [bool]         TF32 in float32 matmuls and cuDNN convolutions on
                        Ampere and newer GPUs. (default: True)
  --num_workers int     Number of workers for the dataloader. (default: 4)
  --batch_size int      
  --prefetch_factor int
  --persistent_workers bool
  --dataloader_multiprocessing_context [str]
                        DataLoader worker start method. "spawn" is safer than
                        "fork" with non-fork-safe libs (PyAV / torchcodec /
                        ffmpeg), but adds some worker-startup time per run
                        since workers re-import modules instead of inheriting
                        parent state. Override with
                        `--dataloader_multiprocessing_context=fork` when
                        appropriate, or set it to `null` to use Python's
                        platform default. (default: spawn)
  --steps int           
  --env_eval_freq int   Run policy in the simulation environment every N steps
                        to measure reward/success (0 = disabled). (default:
                        20000)
  --log_freq int        0 or negative disables periodic logging (default: 200)
  --eval_steps int      Compute eval loss on held-out episodes every N steps
                        (0 = disabled). Requires eval_split > 0. (default: 0)
  --max_eval_samples int
                        Cap on total eval samples, split uniformly across
                        tasks (0 = use all held-out data). (default: 0)
  --tolerance_s float   
  --save_checkpoint bool
  --save_freq int       Checkpoint is saved every `save_freq` training
                        iterations and after the last training step. A non-
                        positive value disables periodic saving, keeping only
                        the final checkpoint. (default: 20000)
  --checkpoint_format CheckpointFormat
                        Model-artifact format inside checkpoints; non-default
                        values require a sharded run. (default:
                        CheckpointFormat.SAFETENSORS)
  --use_policy_training_preset bool
  --save_checkpoint_to_hub bool
                        Push each saved checkpoint to the Hub (policy.repo_id)
                        as it is written, not just the final model (useful to
                        monitor progress mid-run). Optional; the final model
                        is pushed regardless. Works the same locally and
                        remotely. (default: False)
  --rename_map dict[str,str]
                        Rename map for the observation to override the image
                        and state keys (default: {})

DatasetConfig ['dataset']:

  --dataset.repo_id str
                        You may provide a list of datasets here. `train.py`
                        creates them all and concatenates them. Note: only
                        data keys common between the datasets are kept. Each
                        dataset gets and additional transform that inserts the
                        "dataset_index" into the returned item. The index
                        mapping is made according to the order in which the
                        datasets are provided. (default: None)
  --dataset.repo_type str
                        Hub repository type: "dataset" (default) or "bucket"
                        for an HF Storage Bucket (hf://buckets/). Whether a
                        bucket needs streaming=true depends on the dataset's
                        storage format, so that is checked at load time in the
                        dataset factory. (default: dataset)
  --dataset.root [str]  Root directory for a concrete local dataset tree (e.g.
                        'dataset/path'). If None, local datasets are looked up
                        under $HF_LEROBOT_HOME/repo_id and Hub downloads use a
                        revision-safe cache under $HF_LEROBOT_HOME/hub. With
                        streaming=true, an 'hf://buckets/OWNER/BUCKET' URI is
                        also accepted and implies repo_type="bucket".
                        (default: None)
  --dataset.episodes [list[int]]
  --dataset.exclude_episodes [list[int]]
                        Episode indices to drop (e.g. corrupt or heterogeneous
                        ones). Applied on top of `episodes`. (default: None)
  --dataset.revision [str]
  --dataset.use_imagenet_stats bool
  --dataset.video_backend str
  --dataset.return_uint8 bool
                        When True, RGB video frames are returned as uint8
                        tensors (0-255) instead of float32 (0.0-1.0). This
                        reduces memory and speeds up DataLoader IPC. The
                        training pipeline handles the conversion. (default:
                        False)
  --dataset.depth_output_unit str
                        Physical unit depth maps are dequantized to at load
                        time: "mm" (millimeters) or "m" (metres). Has no
                        effect on datasets without depth cameras. (default:
                        mm)
  --dataset.streaming bool
  --dataset.streaming_episode_pool_size [int]
                        Complete episodes mixed by the exact-coverage sampler
                        of each DataLoader worker. None mixes 32 episodes for
                        the rank and gives each of the N workers 32/N; a
                        larger pool mixes more episodes in each batch, but
                        uses more memory and fetches more data before the
                        first sample. (default: None)
  --dataset.streaming_sampling_strategy StreamingSamplingStrategy
                        Round-robin trades frame-weighted sampling for more
                        even resident-episode mixing. (default:
                        StreamingSamplingStrategy.REMAINING)
  --dataset.streaming_prefetch_episodes int
                        Complete episodes fetched ahead of the current
                        admission frontier. (default: 8)
  --dataset.streaming_byte_budget_gb float
                        Hard per-rank cap for synthesized episode-video bytes.
                        (default: 8.0)
  --dataset.streaming_decode_threads int
                        Parallel sample assembly/decode workers and their
                        bounded in-order result queue. (default: 2)
  --dataset.streaming_decoded_queue_size int
  --dataset.streaming_native_http_connections [int]
                        Per-rank native HTTP limits. None preserves the
                        fetcher's worker-derived default. (default: None)
  --dataset.streaming_native_http_subranges int
  --dataset.streaming_sidecar_lock_timeout_s float
                        Seconds to wait for another process that builds the
                        same MP4 sidecar. (default: 1800)
  --dataset.video_decoder_cache_size [int]
                        Maximum open video decoders. Streaming: per rank, None
                        covers every camera in the episode pool. Map-style:
                        only for non-default storage formats (e.g. lance), per
                        DataLoader worker. (default: None)
  --dataset.eval_split float
                        Fraction of episodes held out per task for offline
                        evaluation (0.0 = disabled). (default: 0.0)

ImageTransformsConfig ['dataset.image_transforms']:
  
      These transforms are all using standard torchvision.transforms.v2
      You can find out how these transformations affect images here:
      https://pytorch.org/vision/0.18/auto_examples/transforms/plot_transforms_illustrations.html
      `BatchedRandomSubsetApply` samples them per frame.
      

  --dataset.image_transforms.enable bool
                        Set this flag to `true` to enable transforms during
                        training (default: False)
  --dataset.image_transforms.backend {dataloader,gpu}
                        Where the transforms run. "dataloader" applies them
                        per sample in the DataLoader workers (CPU). "gpu"
                        leaves the workers to decode only and applies the
                        batched, per-sample equivalents on the policy device
                        inside the training preprocessor; see
                        `BatchedImageTransforms` for what is supported. The
                        knobs below sit next to `enable` and `tfs` because
                        they describe how the dataset's transforms run, and
                        every consumer of a dataset config that enables them
                        can then run them unchanged. (default: dataloader)
  --dataset.image_transforms.gpu_compile bool
                        "gpu" backend only. torch.compile the batched
                        transforms: about three times faster per batch for a
                        one-off compile of 15-30 s per frame shape (a second,
                        dynamic compile covers the epoch's partial last batch
                        and the chunk remainders). Set to False if compilation
                        is unavailable on the machine. This does not change
                        the augmentation: the random parameters are drawn
                        outside the compiled function. (default: True)
  --dataset.image_transforms.gpu_chunk_size [int]
                        "gpu" backend only. Augment this many samples at a
                        time. Every configured transform runs on the whole
                        chunk and is masked into the samples that drew it, so
                        the peak memory is two float copies of the batch (the
                        input conversion and the output) plus about four
                        copies of the chunk compiled, ten eager. At 256x256
                        with two frames per sample that is 0.5 GB for a batch
                        of 160 at the default against 1.1 GB unbounded; at
                        480x640, 2.4 GB against 6.3 GB. Chunking does not
                        change the augmentation either, since the parameters
                        are drawn for the whole batch and sliced per chunk.
                        None augments the whole batch at once. (default: 32)
  --dataset.image_transforms.max_num_transforms int
                        This is the maximum number of transforms (sampled from
                        these below) that will be applied to each frame. It's
                        an integer in the interval [1,
                        number_of_available_transforms]. (default: 3)
  --dataset.image_transforms.random_order bool
                        By default, transforms are applied in Torchvision's
                        suggested order (shown below). Set this to True to
                        apply them in a random order. (default: False)
  --dataset.image_transforms.tfs dict[str,ImageTransformConfig]

Optional ['env']:

EnvConfig ['env']:

  --env.type {aloha,pusht,gym_manipulator,libero,metaworld,robocasa,vlabench,isaaclab_arena,unitree_g1_mujoco,libero_plus,robotwin,robomme}
                        Which type of EnvConfig ['env'] to use (default: None)

Optional ['policy']:

PreTrainedConfig ['policy']:
  
      Base configuration class for policy models.
  
      Args:
          n_obs_steps: Number of environment steps worth of observations to pass to the policy (takes the
              current step and additional steps going back).
          input_features: A dictionary defining the PolicyFeature of the input data for the policy. The key represents
              the input data name, and the value is PolicyFeature, which consists of FeatureType and shape attributes.
          output_features: A dictionary defining the PolicyFeature of the output data for the policy. The key represents
              the output data name, and the value is PolicyFeature, which consists of FeatureType and shape attributes.
          normalization_mapping: A dictionary that maps from a str value of FeatureType (e.g., "STATE", "VISUAL") to
              a corresponding NormalizationMode (e.g., NormalizationMode.MIN_MAX)
      

  --policy.type {act,diffusion,dm05,eo1,evo1,fastwam,pi05,fineart_vla,flux3,gaussian_actor,groot,lawam,lingbot_va,lingbot_vla_v2,longwam,molmoact2,multi_task_dit,pi0,pi0_fast,smolvla,tdmpc,vla_jepa,vqbet,wall_oss_05,wall_x,xvla}
                        Which type of PreTrainedConfig ['policy'] to use
                        (default: None)

Optional ['reward_model']:

RewardModelConfig ['reward_model']:
  Base configuration for reward models.
  
      Args:
      input_features: A dictionary defining the PolicyFeature of the input data for the reward. The key represents
          the input data name, and the value is PolicyFeature, which consists of FeatureType and shape attributes.
      output_features: A dictionary defining the PolicyFeature of the output data for the reward. The key represents
          the output data name, and the value is PolicyFeature, which consists of FeatureType and shape attributes.
      

  --reward_model.type {reward_classifier,robometer,sarm,topreward}
                        Which type of RewardModelConfig ['reward_model'] to
                        use (default: None)

Optional ['optimizer']:

  --optimizer.type {adam,adamw,sgd,xvla-adamw,multi_adam,molmoact2_adamw}
                        Which type of OptimizerConfig ['optimizer'] to use
                        (default: None)

Optional ['scheduler']:

LRSchedulerConfig ['scheduler']:

  --scheduler.type {diffuser,vqbet,constant_with_warmup,cosine_annealing_with_warmup,cosine_decay_with_warmup,frozen_warmup_constant,warmup_stable_decay,lawam_cosine_with_min_lr,molmoact2_cosine_with_warmup}
                        Which type of LRSchedulerConfig ['scheduler'] to use
                        (default: None)

ParallelismConfig ['parallelism']:
  Process topology: dp_replicate / dp_shard (HSDP) and context-parallel degree placeholders.

  --parallelism.dp_replicate int
  --parallelism.dp_shard int
                        -1 is an explicit opt-in sentinel: shard over
                        world_size // (dp_replicate * cp). (default: 1)
  --parallelism.cfg_parallel int
                        Classifier-free-guidance parallelism — inference-only
                        (cosmos/vllm-omni precedent: cond/uncond branches on
                        different ranks). Reserved for the serving round;
                        training validates it to 1. Meaningful values are 1 or
                        2 (Cosmos3 has two CFG branches). (default: 1)

ContextParallelConfig ['parallelism.context_parallel']:
  Ring x Ulysses context parallelism (sequence parallelism for attention).
  
      Both degrees are configured placeholders in this release: the CP engine is not implemented
      yet, and enabling either degree > 1 fails fast at config validation. The fields exist now so
      that the CLI surface, checkpoint metadata, and mesh math are stable when the engine lands.
      

  --parallelism.context_parallel.ring_degree int
  --parallelism.context_parallel.ulysses_degree int

AcceleratorConfig ['accelerator']:
  Execution runtime handed to the Accelerator: mixed precision, gradient accumulation,
  FSDP/DDP tuning knobs, compile & activation-checkpointing placeholders.

  --accelerator.mixed_precision str

GradientAccumulationConfig ['accelerator.gradient_accumulation']:
  Mirror of the `GradientAccumulationPlugin` subset LeRobot supports.
  
      The step count and ``sync_each_batch`` are the knobs. ``sync_with_dataloader`` is pinned to
      False by :meth:`build_plugin`: the training loop cycles a finite dataloader, so accelerate's
      default of syncing at every dataloader end would force an optimizer step at every dataset
      epoch boundary instead of every ``steps`` micro-batches.
      

  --accelerator.gradient_accumulation.steps int
  --accelerator.gradient_accumulation.sync_each_batch bool
                        Reduce the gradients at every micro-batch instead of
                        only at the last one. (default: False)

GradScalerConfig ['accelerator.grad_scaler']:
  Mirror of the `GradScalerKwargs` subset LeRobot exposes — fp16's loss scaler.
  
      Inert unless `mixed_precision="fp16"`: accelerate reads this handler only on the branch
      that builds the `torch.amp.GradScaler`. The defaults are accelerate's (and torch's) own.
  
      `enabled` is deliberately not mirrored. fp16 without loss scaling underflows gradients to
      zero and diverges, so a disabled scaler is never a valid LeRobot configuration; runs that
      want no scaling want `mixed_precision="bf16"` instead.
      

  --accelerator.grad_scaler.init_scale float
  --accelerator.grad_scaler.growth_factor float
  --accelerator.grad_scaler.backoff_factor float
  --accelerator.grad_scaler.growth_interval int

FSDPConfig ['accelerator.fsdp']:
  Mirror of the `FullyShardedDataParallelPlugin` subset LeRobot supports (FSDP2 only).
  
      Exactly one wrap policy applies: `wrap_modules` (module *class names* forming the FSDP
      units — and, later, the activation-checkpointing units) or `min_num_params` (size-based).
      When both are None, the policy's own `_fsdp_wrap_modules` declaration is used; a run where
      no wrap source exists at all fails loudly rather than silently wrapping only the root.
      

  --accelerator.fsdp.reshard_after_forward bool
  --accelerator.fsdp.wrap_modules [list[str]]
  --accelerator.fsdp.min_num_params [int]
  --accelerator.fsdp.cpu_offload bool
  --accelerator.fsdp.ignored_modules [str]
                        Regex matched against module FQNs to exclude their
                        parameters from sharding. (default: None)

MixedPrecisionPolicyConfig ['accelerator.fsdp.mixed_precision_policy']:
  Mirror of `torch.distributed.fsdp.MixedPrecisionPolicy`, applied to every FSDP2 unit.
  
      At torch's defaults no policy is built and accelerate derives one from `mixed_precision`.
      Otherwise the policy is built from these four fields alone.
      

  --accelerator.fsdp.mixed_precision_policy.param_dtype [dtype]
                        Dtype of the unsharded parameters: the forward, the
                        backward and the all-gather. None keeps their dtype.
                        (default: None)
  --accelerator.fsdp.mixed_precision_policy.reduce_dtype [dtype]
                        Dtype of the gradient reduction. None follows
                        `param_dtype`. (default: None)
  --accelerator.fsdp.mixed_precision_policy.output_dtype [dtype]
                        Dtype every FSDP unit casts its floating-point outputs
                        to. None leaves them unchanged. (default: None)
  --accelerator.fsdp.mixed_precision_policy.cast_forward_inputs bool
                        Cast the floating-point forward inputs of every FSDP
                        unit to `param_dtype`. (default: True)

DDPConfig ['accelerator.ddp']:
  Mirror of the `DistributedDataParallelKwargs` subset LeRobot exposes.

  --accelerator.ddp.find_unused_parameters bool
                        Today's in-script default, kept for models with
                        conditional computation. (default: True)
  --accelerator.ddp.gradient_as_bucket_view bool
  --accelerator.ddp.static_graph bool

CompileConfig ['accelerator.compile']:
  torch.compile knobs — a configured placeholder: wiring lands in a later round.
  
      The setup-order contract it will follow is already fixed: compile applies
      after CP dispatch install and activation checkpointing, before `fully_shard`, regionally
      (per wrap unit) — the only combination proven with FSDP2.
      

  --accelerator.compile.enabled bool
  --accelerator.compile.backend str
  --accelerator.compile.mode [str]
  --accelerator.compile.regional bool

ActivationCheckpointingConfig ['accelerator.activation_checkpointing']:
  Activation-checkpointing knobs — a configured placeholder: wiring lands in a later round.
  
      AC units will coincide with the FSDP wrap units (one declaration drives both), applied
      before torch.compile and `fully_shard` (the same ordering contract as CompileConfig).
      

  --accelerator.activation_checkpointing.mode ActivationCheckpointingMode

EvalConfig ['eval']:

  --eval.n_episodes int
  --eval.batch_size int
                        `batch_size` specifies the number of environments to
                        use in a gym.vector.VectorEnv. Set to 0 for auto-
                        tuning based on available CPU cores and n_episodes.
                        (default: 0)
  --eval.use_async_envs bool
                        `use_async_envs` specifies whether to use asynchronous
                        environments (multiprocessing). Defaults to True;
                        automatically downgraded to SyncVectorEnv when
                        batch_size=1. (default: True)
  --eval.recording bool
                        Whether to record eval rollouts as a LeRobot dataset
                        on disk. (default: False)
  --eval.recording_repo_id [str]
                        If set, push recorded eval datasets to the Hub under
                        this repo id (one repo per task, suffixed by task and
                        env index). Requires recording=true. (default: None)
  --eval.recording_private bool
                        Whether the pushed recording repositories should be
                        private. (default: False)

Optional ['ema']:
  EMA of the trainable policy weights, enabled with --ema.type (see EMAConfig). In-training env eval and the
  pushed main branch use the EMA weights.

EMAConfig ['ema']:
  EMA of the trainable policy weights, enabled with --ema.type (see EMAConfig). In-training env eval and the
  pushed main branch use the EMA weights.

  --ema.type {warmup,constant,power}
                        Which type of EMAConfig ['ema'] to use (default: None)

TrackioConfig ['trackio']:
  Training run tracking with Trackio (https://huggingface.co/docs/trackio).
  
      Runs are stored in a local SQLite database under `~/.cache/huggingface/trackio` and viewed with
      `trackio show --project <project>`. Set `space_id` to sync the run to a Hugging Face Space instead.
      

  --trackio.enable bool
  --trackio.disable_artifact bool
                        Opt in with False to duplicate checkpoint weights in
                        Trackio; Hub uploads are configured separately.
                        (default: True)
  --trackio.project str
  --trackio.space_id [str]
                        Hugging Face Space (`user/space`) to log to instead of
                        the local database; created if missing. Required for
                        remote jobs (--job.target), whose local database
                        vanishes with the pod. (default: None)
  --trackio.private [bool]
                        Whether a newly created Space is private. Ignored if
                        the Space already exists. (default: None)
  --trackio.run_name [str]
                        Run name. Defaults to "<job_name>-<short id>",
                        persisted in the checkpoint so resuming reattaches to
                        it. (default: None)
  --trackio.resume [str]
                        Allowed values: 'allow', 'must', 'never'. Defaults to
                        'allow' when resuming a checkpoint that stored a
                        run_name (reattach if the run exists, else start a new
                        run under that name) and to 'never' otherwise.
                        (default: None)
  --trackio.capture_console bool
                        Store the run's console output (stdout and stderr, so
                        prints, logs and tracebacks) with the run, viewable
                        and downloadable from its dashboard page. The launch
                        command is recorded either way. (default: True)

Optional ['peft']:

PeftConfig ['peft']:

  --peft.target_modules [list[str]|str]
                        PEFT offers many fine-tuning methods, layer adapters
                        being the most common and currently also the most
                        effective methods so we'll focus on those in this
                        high-level config interface. Either a string (module
                        name suffix or 'all-linear'), a list of module name
                        suffixes or a regular expression describing module
                        names to target with the configured PEFT method. Some
                        policies have a default value for this so that you
                        don't *have* to choose which layers to adapt but it
                        might still be worthwhile depending on your case.
                        (default: None)
  --peft.full_training_modules [list[str]]
                        Names/suffixes of modules to fully fine-tune and store
                        alongside adapter weights. Useful for layers that are
                        not part of a pre-trained model (e.g., action state
                        projections). Depending on the policy this defaults to
                        layers that are newly created in pre-trained policies.
                        If you're fine-tuning an already trained policy you
                        might want to set this to `[]`. Corresponds to PEFT's
                        `modules_to_save`. (default: None)
  --peft.method_type str
                        The PEFT (adapter) method to apply to the policy.
                        Needs to be a valid PEFT type. (default: LORA)
  --peft.init_type [str]
                        Adapter initialization method. Look at the specific
                        PEFT adapter documentation for defaults. (default:
                        None)
  --peft.r int          We expect that all PEFT adapters are in some way doing
                        rank-decomposition therefore this parameter specifies
                        the rank used for the adapter. In general a higher
                        rank means more trainable parameters and closer to
                        full fine-tuning. (default: 16)
  --peft.lora_alpha [int]
                        Alpha parameter for LoRA scaling (scaling = lora_alpha
                        / r). In general, a higher alpha means stronger
                        adaptation signal. If None, the PEFT library defaults
                        to alpha=8, which may dampen high-rank adapters.
                        Common values are r (alpha == rank) or 2*r. (default:
                        None)

JobConfig ['job']:
  Where to run training (local default, or an HF Jobs flavor). See JobConfig.

  --job.target [str]    Where training runs. None (omitted) or "local" runs on
                        this machine. Any other value is an HF Jobs flavor and
                        submits the run to HF Jobs. List available flavors +
                        pricing with `hf jobs hardware` command. (default:
                        None)
  --job.image str       Runtime image for the remote job (ignored for local
                        runs). (default: huggingface/lerobot-gpu:latest)
  --job.timeout [str]   Max wall-clock for the remote job as an HF Jobs
                        duration string (e.g. "2h"). Defaults to "2d": We pass
                        an explicit, generous cap instead. Set a smaller value
                        to fail fast, or a larger one for long runs. (default:
                        2d)
  --job.detach bool     Submit and exit instead of streaming the job logs in
                        the foreground. (default: False)
  --job.tags list[str]  Extra tags attached to the HF job and to any dataset
                        this run pushes to the Hub. A "lerobot" tag is always
                        added; e.g. --job.tags '["lelab"]' adds more.
                        (default: [])

Optional ['sample_weighting']:
  Sample weighting configuration (e.g., for RA-BC training)

SampleWeightingConfig ['sample_weighting']:
  Sample weighting configuration (e.g., for RA-BC training)

  --sample_weighting.type str
  --sample_weighting.progress_path [str]
  --sample_weighting.head_mode str
  --sample_weighting.kappa float
  --sample_weighting.epsilon float
  --sample_weighting.extra_params dict
                        Additional type-specific params can be added here or
                        passed via extra_params (default: {})
